title: Did Hollywood Writers Get Their Happy Ending?

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是本杰明·普林，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 回想一下，早在黑胶唱片时代我在夜总会打碟的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你要带 300 件你最珍视的宝贝去上班，你把 DJ 台变成了一个美丽的、有 50 年历史的文物的微型快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼表推出的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: After 148 days on strike, one of the longest in history,
sentences.zh: 在经历罢工 148 天之后，这是历史上最长的罢工之一，

sentences.en: writers for movies and televisions will return to work today with a deal in hand that amounts to a major win for organized labor in Hollywood.
sentences.zh: 电影和电视编剧将于今天重返工作岗位，并达成了一项协议，这对好莱坞的有组织劳工来说是一场重大胜利。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague John Koblin on why the studios acquiesced and what the deal means for the future of American entertainment.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事约翰·科布林将为你讲述制片厂为何妥协，以及这项协议对美国娱乐业的未来意味着什么。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, September 27th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 9 月 27 日，星期三。

sentences.en: So, John, we're talking on Tuesday afternoon and by all accounts, the writers and the studios have reached a deal on a contract after the writers striking for months and months.
sentences.zh: 所以，约翰，我们在周二下午进行录制，据各方报道，在编剧们进行了长达数月的罢工之后，编剧和制片厂已经就一份合同达成了一项协议。

sentences.en: And we wanted to come to you to talk about this and, you know, how this deal came about, what's actually in it.
sentences.zh: 我们想找你来聊聊这件事，你知道的，这项协议是怎么达成的，里面到底包含些什么。

sentences.en: But right off the bat, top line, highest level, what's your read on all of this?
sentences.zh: 但开门见山地说，最核心的、最高层面的，你对这一切有什么看法？

sentences.en: Who's really the winner here?
sentences.zh: 这里真正的赢家是谁？

sentences.en: It looks like at this moment that the writers really prevailed.
sentences.zh: 目前看来，编剧们确实大获全胜。

sentences.en: You know, it's funny, when the writers last went on strike, which was 15 years ago, 100-day strike, so more than three months.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣，上一次编剧罢工是在 15 年前，那是一场持续 100 天的罢工，也就是三个多月。

sentences.en: After that strike had ended, after they reached that tentative agreement, the guild leader sent out an email that said something like, you know,
sentences.zh: 在那次罢工结束后，在他们达成初步协议后，工会领袖发了一封邮件，内容大概是，

sentences.en: we didn't get everything we wanted and, you know, we've sacrificed countless hours during the struggle, but we did well.
sentences.zh: 我们没有得到我们想要的一切，而且，你知道，在这场斗争中我们牺牲了无数个小时，但我们干得不错。

sentences.en: This time, when they announced the tentative agreement, which was on Sunday night, I mean, it was like vibrating with excitement, that message.
sentences.zh: 这一次，当他们宣布达成初步协议时——那是在周日晚上——我的意思是，那个消息简直充满了兴奋的颤抖。

sentences.en: It makes me very excited because I think we might have actually saved the film and TV industry with this strike.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到非常兴奋，因为我认为我们可能真的通过这次罢工拯救了电影和电视行业。

sentences.en: They came out and said, we say this with great pride, that this deal is exceptional.
sentences.zh: 他们出来说，我们无比自豪地宣布，这项协议是杰出的。

sentences.en: There has been so much at stake, and they would not settle for a subpar deal because we're not settling over here.
sentences.zh: 这次的赌注太大了，他们不会满足于一份 subpar 的协议，因为我们不会在这里妥协。

sentences.en: So there is a perception within the writers' guilt that they got a big W, like capital W, like capital V for victory.
sentences.zh: 因此，在编剧工会内部有一种看法，认为他们赢得了一场大胜，带有大写的 W，就像大写的 V 代表胜利一样。

sentences.en: Capital V for victory for the writers.
sentences.zh: 这是编剧们大写的胜利。

sentences.en: And we've talked about this before, John, on the show, but just remind us what it was that they had wanted.
sentences.zh: 约翰，我们在节目中以前也讨论过这一点，但请提醒我们，他们一直想要的是什么。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, the strike has been framed in pretty epic terms, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，这场罢工被定性为具有史诗般的意义，对吧？

sentences.en: A showdown over what it really means to be a creative force in the era of the streaming revolution,
sentences.zh: 这是一场关于在流媒体革命时代，作为创意力量究竟意味着什么的对决，

sentences.en: when the technology and the economics of the entire industry have been changing before our eyes.
sentences.zh: 当时整个行业的科技和经济都在我们眼前发生着变化。

sentences.en: But nitty gritty, what were the writers asking for?
sentences.zh: 但具体到细节，编剧们到底在要求什么？

sentences.en: Epic is one way to describe it.
sentences.zh: 史诗般是形容它的一种方式。

sentences.en: Another way they described it was, literally, this is existential.
sentences.zh: 他们形容它的另一种方式是，字面意思，这关乎生死存亡。

sentences.en: This moment is existential.
sentences.zh: 这个时刻关乎生死存亡。

sentences.en: We are fighting for our survival.
sentences.zh: 我们在为生存而战。

sentences.en: But by far, the biggest issue was compensation.
sentences.zh: 但到目前为止，最大的问题还是报酬。

sentences.en: We talked about this last time, but let's go back 20, 30 years ago, back to the network TV days.
sentences.zh: 我们上次讨论过这个，但让我们回到 20、30 年前，回到电视网黄金时期。

sentences.en: If you created an ER, a big, big hit, hundreds of episodes, even if it ends after, say, nine or ten seasons, it's going to live forever.
sentences.zh: 如果你创作了一部《急诊室的故事》，一部非常非常热门、拥有数百集的作品，即使它在比如说九到十季后结束，它也将长盛不衰。

sentences.en: And the reason is it's going to go into syndication.
sentences.zh: 原因在于它将进入联合发行。

sentences.en: It's going to go into cable.
sentences.zh: 它将进入有线电视。

sentences.en: It's going to go into repeats, essentially.
sentences.zh: 本质上，它将进入重播环节。

sentences.en: And every time that would air on, say, a cable network like TBS, if you were a writer of an episode, you got a check.
sentences.zh: 每当它在诸如 TBS 这样的有线电视网络上播出时，如果你是其中一集的编剧，你就能拿到一张支票。

sentences.en: So that's just money in the bank.
sentences.zh: 所以这简直就是稳赚不赔的钱。

sentences.en: You bring that back.
sentences.zh: 你把这笔钱拿回来。

sentences.en: Kind of like a royalty.
sentences.zh: 有点像版税。

sentences.en: Kind of like a royalty.
sentences.zh: 有点像版税。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So now let's look at the streaming era.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们来看看流媒体时代。

sentences.en: If you create a hit show on Netflix, let's say, Bridgerton, you get a nice amount of money up front after they greenlit the show.
sentences.zh: 如果你在 Netflix 上创作了一部热门剧集，比方说《布里奇顿》，在他们批准立项后，你会预先拿到一笔相当可观的资金。

sentences.en: That's great.
sentences.zh: 这很棒。

sentences.en: But then even if you have a mega success like a Bridgerton, if you think about a place like Netflix, there's no syndication.
sentences.zh: 但即便你获得了像《布里奇顿》这样的巨大成功，如果你想想 Netflix 这样的平台，是没有联合发行的。

sentences.en: It just stays on Netflix.
sentences.zh: 它只留在 Netflix 上。

sentences.en: They're not licensing it to a cable network.
sentences.zh: 他们不会把它授权给有线电视网络。

sentences.en: So the money you used to get after a show was a huge hit, that doesn't really exist in the same way.
sentences.zh: 所以，以前在剧集大获成功后你能拿到的钱，现在已经不复存在了，形式完全不同了。

sentences.en: So writers are essentially asking for more money in several different places from the studios.
sentences.zh: 因此，编剧们本质上是在要求制片厂在几个不同的方面提供更多的资金。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So more pay was really the number one issue.
sentences.zh: 所以更高的薪酬确实是头号问题。

sentences.en: What else were they asking for?
sentences.zh: 他们还在要求什么？

sentences.en: They also wanted a little bit of transparency.
sentences.zh: 他们还想要一点透明度。

sentences.en: Again, if we look back 20, 25 years ago, we know how many people watched that episode of Friends or Seinfeld or ER.
sentences.zh: 同样，如果我们回看 20、25 年前，我们知道有多少人观看了那一集的《老友记》、《宋飞正传》或《急诊室的故事》。

sentences.en: Nielsen used to tell you how many millions of viewers were watching it.
sentences.zh: 尼尔森过去会告诉你到底有多少百万观众在观看它。

sentences.en: We do not have that same level of transparency from an Amazon or Hulu or a Netflix.
sentences.zh: 我们从亚马逊、Hulu 或 Netflix 那里得不到同等水平的透明度。

sentences.en: Though presumably they know it, given the fact that it's clicks, right?
sentences.zh: 尽管考虑到这是按点击量计算的，他们大概是知道的，对吧？

sentences.en: For sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: They definitely know it.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对知道。

sentences.en: And, like, they'll give us something these days where here's our top 10 in the United States today.
sentences.zh: 而且，比如，现在他们会给我们一些数据，比如这是今天美国的前 10 名榜单。

sentences.en: But the writers, they wanted to know that if a show is a mega hit, like, we want to profit from that, too.
sentences.zh: 但编剧们希望知道，如果一部剧集大获成功，我们也希望从中分一杯羹。

sentences.en: That's the way the old system used to work.
sentences.zh: 这正是旧系统运作的方式。

sentences.en: And the other interesting thing they were asking for was about AI.
sentences.zh: 他们要求的另一个有趣的事情是关于人工智能的。

sentences.en: And what exactly were they asking for when it comes to AI?
sentences.zh: 他们在人工智能方面到底在要求什么？

sentences.en: I mean, there were several different things, but let's focus on one, which is if I'm a studio executive and I have a stack of Nora Ephron scripts, she wrote You've Got Mail,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有好几个不同的方面，但让我们专注于一个，那就是如果我是制片厂高管，我有一叠诺拉·埃夫伦的剧本，她写过《电子情书》，

sentences.en: for instance.
sentences.zh: 举个例子。

sentences.en: Famous writer.
sentences.zh: 著名的作家。

sentences.en: Among many other great movies.
sentences.zh: 她还创作了许多其他优秀的电影。

sentences.en: But I take those scripts, I feed them into the AI robot, and I say, give me a Nora Ephron style of a rom-com, of a romantic comedy.
sentences.zh: 但我拿着这些剧本，把它们喂给人工智能机器人，然后我说，给我写一部诺拉·埃夫伦风格的浪漫喜剧。

sentences.en: That is the writer's worst nightmare because they don't want a robot to be the accredited writer of a movie.
sentences.zh: 那是编剧们的噩梦，因为他们不希望机器人成为电影的署名字体编剧。

sentences.en: So, no good.
sentences.zh: 所以，这可不行。

sentences.en: No bueno.
sentences.zh: 绝对不行。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't want a robot to be an accredited writer of my article.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我也不希望机器人成为我文章的署名字体作者。

sentences.en: I mean, this is, like, kind of scary, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这感觉有点吓人，对吧？

sentences.en: Robots should not be replacing writers.
sentences.zh: 机器人不应该取代编剧。

sentences.en: That feels reasonable to me as well.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这也很合理。

sentences.en: I feel tribal about this.
sentences.zh: 我对这件事有强烈的同仇敌忾感。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's the basic list of things the writers were asking for.
sentences.zh: 好的，这就是编剧们要求的基本清单。

sentences.en: And now, Tuesday afternoon, we are about to live into the answer of what they got.
sentences.zh: 现在，在周二下午，我们将亲眼见证他们得到了什么的答案。

sentences.en: What do we know about what they did get?
sentences.zh: 关于他们到底得到了什么，我们知道些什么？

sentences.en: So, it's going to become more clear in the coming days.
sentences.zh: 所以，在接下来的几天里，情况会变得更加明朗。

sentences.en: But we know that they got a lot.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道他们得到了很多。

sentences.en: We know they got much of what they asked for.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们得到了他们要求的大部分内容。

sentences.en: And, you know, we were talking about their statement vibrating with joy earlier.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们刚才还在讨论他们早先那份洋溢着喜悦的声明。

sentences.en: Exactly, right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，对吧？

sentences.en: The studio's only statement was the Writers Guild of America, the Writers' Union, and the Studio Alliance have reached a tentative agreement.
sentences.zh: 制片厂唯一的声明是美国编剧工会、编剧工会和制片厂联盟已经达成了一项初步协议。

sentences.en: Period.
sentences.zh: 句号。

sentences.en: Full stop.
sentences.zh: 到此为止。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就这样。

sentences.en: It was pretty muted.
sentences.zh: 显得相当低调。

sentences.en: So, they gave up a lot more than they were anticipating five months ago.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们放弃的比五个月前预期的要多得多。

sentences.en: And the union, they said they made meaningful gains and protections for every writer in every sector of the union membership.
sentences.zh: 而工会表示，他们为工会成员中各个领域的每一位编剧争取到了有意义的利益和保障。

sentences.en: Translation, we got a lot of what we wanted.
sentences.zh: 翻译一下，我们得到了很多我们想要的东西。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay, so the studios checked all the boxes that they'd put out there.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以制片厂满足了他们提出的所有条件。

sentences.en: How do you explain such a victory for the writers?
sentences.zh: 你如何解释编剧们的这种胜利？

sentences.en: Because, I mean, for months, it just didn't seem like the two sides were even talking.
sentences.zh: 因为，我的意思是，几个月来，双方甚至看起来根本没有在对话。

sentences.en: Like, the story was the picket line.
sentences.zh: 就像，报道的焦点全是纠察线。

sentences.en: So, what got everyone back to the negotiating table and ultimately to a deal?
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么让每个人都回到了谈判桌前，并最终达成协议的呢？

sentences.en: So, there were a few key moments.
sentences.zh: 这里有几个关键时刻。

sentences.en: So, after the writers go on strike, that's early May.
sentences.zh: 在编剧罢工之后，那是 5 月初。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, the studios have two other contracts to deal with.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，制片厂还有另外两份合同需要处理。

sentences.en: Hollywood directors and then the actors.
sentences.zh: 好莱坞导演，然后是演员。

sentences.en: The studios are not worried about the directors or actors.
sentences.zh: 制片厂并不担心导演或演员。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: The writers have gone on strike many times over the decades.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，编剧已经罢工过很多次了。

sentences.en: They went on strike, as we discussed, 15 years ago.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所讨论的，他们在 15 年前就罢工过。

sentences.en: Before that, they did it in 1988.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，他们在 1988 年这样做过。

sentences.en: Directors and actors, they just have not gone on strike.
sentences.zh: 导演和演员，他们根本没有罢工过。

sentences.en: Like, nearly as many times.
sentences.zh: 次数几乎没那么多。

sentences.en: Last time the actors went on strike was over four decades ago.
sentences.zh: 演员上一次罢工是在四十多年前。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: Okay, so just typically, there's a big difference between these groups.
sentences.zh: 好吧，通常情况下，这些群体之间存在巨大差异。

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: So, the studios negotiate with the directors, get a deal done really quickly.
sentences.zh: 因此，制片厂与导演进行谈判，非常快地达成了一项协议。

sentences.en: The directors call the deal historic.
sentences.zh: 导演们称这项协议具有历史意义。

sentences.en: So, one down, one to go.
sentences.zh: 所以，解决了一个，还有一个。

sentences.en: And then, sure enough, by mid-July, the actors do go on strike.
sentences.zh: 然后，果不其然，到 7 月中旬，演员们真的罢工了。

sentences.en: And it kind of stuns everybody.
sentences.zh: 这让所有人都感到震惊。

sentences.en: Producers, agents, Hollywood observers.
sentences.zh: 制片人、经纪人、好莱坞观察家。

sentences.en: But it also surprises the studio executives.
sentences.zh: 但这同时也让制片厂高管感到意外。

sentences.en: Okay, so the actors go on strike.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以演员罢工了。

sentences.en: But what does that have to do with the writers?
sentences.zh: 但这跟编剧有什么关系？

sentences.en: So, by the time the actors go on strike, the writers have been on strike for two and a half months.
sentences.zh: 因此，当演员罢工时，编剧已经罢工两个半月了。

sentences.en: It's mid-July.
sentences.zh: 那是 7 月中旬。

sentences.en: It's getting hot outside.
sentences.zh: 外面开始变热了。

sentences.en: It's hot in L.A.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶很热。

sentences.en: It's hot in New York.
sentences.zh: 纽约很热。

sentences.en: They've been walking these picket lines for two and a half months.
sentences.zh: 他们已经在这些纠察线上走了两个半月了。

sentences.en: And the actors, surprise strike, because everybody was caught off guard, there's suddenly wind at the backs of the writers.
sentences.zh: 而演员们突然袭击，因为所有人都被打了个措手不及，编剧们身后突然有了一股东风。

sentences.en: They're not so lonely on those picket lines anymore.
sentences.zh: 他们在那些纠察线上不再那么孤单了。

sentences.en: It's this huge moment of solidarity.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的声援时刻。

sentences.en: The actors and writers, they hadn't been on strike at the same time, going back generations.
sentences.zh: 演员和编剧，他们几代人以来都没有同时罢工过。

sentences.en: It was since 1960.
sentences.zh: 自 1960 年以来就没有过。

sentences.en: So, it had been years.
sentences.zh: 所以已经很多年了。

sentences.en: And that is what shut down Hollywood, because all of a sudden, cameras can't roll anymore.
sentences.zh: 正是这一点让好莱坞陷入了停顿，因为突然之间，摄像机无法再运转了。

sentences.en: You can't work without actors.
sentences.zh: 没有演员你没法工作。

sentences.en: It got the attention of everybody.
sentences.zh: 这引起了所有人的注意。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, Hollywood is at a total standstill, right?
sentences.zh: 现在，好莱坞陷入了完全瘫痪的状态，对吧？

sentences.en: No one can work.
sentences.zh: 没有人能工作。

sentences.en: Including, by the way, John, my own brother, who works in the film industry.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，其中也包括我的亲弟弟，约翰，他在电影行业工作。

sentences.en: He takes photographs on film sets.

sentences.zh: 电影也会减少。

sentences.en: You will find yourself on your couch at some point, clicking on all these streaming services, saying to yourself, where is something new to watch?
sentences.zh: 你会发现自己在某个时刻坐在沙发上，点着所有这些流媒体服务，心里纳闷：哪里有新鲜的节目可看？

sentences.en: Like, I want, no, give me more choices.
sentences.zh: 就像，我想要，不，给我更多选择。

sentences.en: I want more choices.
sentences.zh: 我想要更多选择。

sentences.en: And you won't quite have that.
sentences.zh: 而你却无法完全得到满足。

sentences.en: But, John, what if I don't want quite so many choices?
sentences.zh: 但是，约翰，如果我不想有那么多选择呢？

sentences.en: I mean, maybe there's an element of silver lining in this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这其中也许有一点一线生机。

sentences.en: I mean, there were so many shows, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，以前有那么多节目，对吧？

sentences.en: Should there be that many shows?
sentences.zh: 真的需要那么多节目吗？

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全赞同。

sentences.en: I mean, this is something, if you put true serum in the arm of creative executives, they will say, fewer shows, that is great.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你给创意高管打一针诚实血清，他们会说，节目少，那太棒了。

sentences.en: Because then we, as creative executives, have time to focus on quality.
sentences.zh: 因为这样我们作为创意高管，就有时间专注于质量。

sentences.en: We have time to really get in there and help writers with their script.
sentences.zh: 我们有时间真正深入进去，帮助编剧完善剧本。

sentences.en: And to help with the cuts of a show.
sentences.zh: 并协助节目的剪辑。

sentences.en: So, yes, I think long-term for consumer, it will be good.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我认为从长远来看对消费者是有好处的。

sentences.en: Because, no, we did not need 600 scripted shows in the United States every single year.
sentences.zh: 因为，不，我们不需要美国每年生产六百部有剧本的节目。

sentences.en: I only watched a fraction of them.
sentences.zh: 我只看了其中的一小部分。

sentences.en: It's hard to watch that much television, even with all the time in the world.
sentences.zh: 要看那么多电视太难了，哪怕你有的是时间。

sentences.en: Perhaps they can focus on the good ones.
sentences.zh: 也许他们可以把精力集中在好的作品上。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, John, it strikes me that this is a moment where the streaming industry has just kind of lived through its heady, young, maybe teenage days, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，约翰，我觉得现在这个时刻，流媒体行业刚刚经历完了它狂热、年轻、或许还有点叛逆的青春期，对吧？

sentences.en: And now we are living into an era in which it has to grow up.
sentences.zh: 而现在我们正步入一个必须成熟的时代。

sentences.en: And in some ways, we, as consumers, also have to grow up along with it.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，我们作为消费者，也必须随之一起成熟。

sentences.en: Which, what I mean by that is, you know, we have to realize that these shows do cost a lot of money to make.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，我们必须意识到制作这些节目确实需要花很多钱。

sentences.en: And that we're going to have to come to terms with the fact that we're going to have fewer of them.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不接受这样一个事实：我们将拥有更少的节目。

sentences.en: And we're going to have to pay more money to get them.
sentences.zh: 而且我们要花更多的钱才能看到它们。

sentences.en: Yeah, I guess maybe we're in sort of our adolescent moment for these streaming services.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这些流媒体服务也许正处于青春期吧。

sentences.en: And as a result, it's a little tricky.
sentences.zh: 因此，情况有点棘手。

sentences.en: It's a little difficult.
sentences.zh: 有点困难。

sentences.en: It's a little tough.
sentences.zh: 有点艰难。

sentences.en: And it's going to be tough for us.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说也将是艰难的。

sentences.en: Because, you know, the whole promise of streaming was this was all going to be so much cheaper, right?
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，流媒体最初的承诺是这一切会便宜得多，对吧？

sentences.en: This is going to be so much cheaper than cable.
sentences.zh: 这比有线电视要便宜得多。

sentences.en: Let's cut the cord, subscribe to a few streaming services, and we're good to go.
sentences.zh: 我们退订有线电视，订阅几个流媒体服务，就万事大吉了。

sentences.en: There's talk in the entertainment industry now of, why don't we bundle a few of these streaming services together?
sentences.zh: 娱乐行业现在有一种说法，为什么我们不把几个流媒体服务捆绑在一起呢？

sentences.en: Max, meet Peacock, meet Paramount+.
sentences.zh: Max，认识一下Peacock，认识一下Paramount+。

sentences.en: So all of a sudden, you're starting to recreate cable in some way.
sentences.zh: 所以突然之间，你开始以某种方式重塑有线电视。

sentences.en: So the cost in the end, it's probably going to approach or maybe even match at some point what we used to pay for for cable.
sentences.zh: 因此，最终的成本可能接近甚至在某种程度上匹配我们过去为有线电视支付的费用。

sentences.en: So, John, thinking about this moment we're in right now with streaming.
sentences.zh: 所以，约翰，回想我们现在所处的这个流媒体时代。

sentences.en: And at the same time, what's emerging from this new contract, it's almost like we're going back in a way to that old model of TV and film.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，从这份新合同中涌现出的东西，几乎就像我们在某种程度上回到了电视和电影的旧模式。

sentences.en: You know, the pre-streaming version where big entertainment companies made fewer shows.
sentences.zh: 你知道，流媒体出现之前的版本，那时大型娱乐公司制作较少的节目。

sentences.en: We paid more, but also the writers got paid more.
sentences.zh: 我们付出了更多，但编剧也得到了更多的报酬。

sentences.en: I mean, the studios would love to go back 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，制片厂很想回到20年前。

sentences.en: The writers would love to go back 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 编剧们也很想回到20年前。

sentences.en: But that world is just gone now.
sentences.zh: 但那个世界现在已经一去不复返了。

sentences.en: Streaming has changed everything.
sentences.zh: 流媒体改变了一切。

sentences.en: This technological change has shifted everything.
sentences.zh: 这场技术变革颠覆了一切。

sentences.en: But in the case of the writer, you know, you're never going to make friends money again.
sentences.zh: 但在编剧的案例中，你知道，你再也赚不到《老友记》那样的巨额财富了。

sentences.en: But if you do create a big hit on Netflix, if you do create, say, a Bridgerton, with this contract, it does set you up a little bit better.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在Netflix上创造了一个大热作品，比如你创作了《布里奇顿》，通过这份合同，你的处境确实会稍微好一点。

sentences.en: You're going to get more money than you did, say, four or five years ago.
sentences.zh: 比起四五年前，你将获得更多的报酬。

sentences.en: But what's kind of interesting on the other side of the strike, the studios are over here, the writers are over there,
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，在罢工的另一边，制片厂在这边，编剧在那边，

sentences.en: and they're both kind of just stumbling their way into the future, trying to make this work.
sentences.zh: 他们都在跌跌撞撞地走向未来，试图让这一切行之有效。

sentences.en: Streaming has changed everything.
sentences.zh: 流媒体改变了一切。

sentences.en: It's upended everything.
sentences.zh: 它颠覆了一切。

sentences.en: And both the studios and the writers are just trying to figure out a way to make it to the other side, when all of a sudden streaming is all that exists,
sentences.zh: 制片厂和编剧都在寻找一种方法，当流媒体成为唯一存在的形式，

sentences.en: and cable television really doesn't exist, or network TV doesn't really exist, that they both still are around.
sentences.zh: 而有线电视或传统电视实际上已不复存在时，他们如何度过难关，其实这两者都还在。编剧仍在写作，制片厂仍在制作新的电视剧和电影。

sentences.en: Writers are still writing, and the studios are still making new TV shows, new movies.
sentences.zh: 编剧仍在写作，制片厂仍在制作新的电视剧和电影。

sentences.en: So the contract, in a way, is pushing our, you know, adolescent, rambunctious streaming out of the house.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，这份合同正在把我们那个充满朝气、吵闹不休的流媒体“青少年”赶出家门。

sentences.en: Streaming goes to college.
sentences.zh: 流媒体要上大学了。

sentences.en: John, thank you.
sentences.zh: 约翰，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: On Tuesday night, the Writers Guild of America made the details of its deal with the studios public for the first time.
sentences.zh: 周二晚上，美国编剧工会首次公开了与各大制片厂达成协议的细节。

sentences.en: It included major concessions on how the writers are paid, including royalties for overseas viewing.
sentences.zh: 其中包括关于编剧薪酬的重大让步，包括海外观看的版税。

sentences.en: It also guaranteed that the studios will not use artificial intelligence to rewrite original material.
sentences.zh: 它还保证制片厂不会使用人工智能来重写原创素材。

sentences.en: The union's 11,500 screenwriter members are expected to approve the three-year deal in a vote that begins on Monday.
sentences.zh: 工会的11500名编剧成员预计将在周一开始的投票中批准这项为期三年的协议。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》游戏板块拼字游戏之一《Connections》的创作者。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天都创作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》这两款游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做色彩联觉的现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到的人这样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问nytimes.com/games开始今天的游戏。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该了解的其他事情。

sentences.en: The legal troubles of former President Donald Trump deepened on Tuesday when a New York judge ruled against him in a civil case filed by New York State Attorney General Letitia James.
sentences.zh: 前总统唐纳德·特朗普的法律麻烦在周二加深，当时纽约一名法官在纽约州总检察长莱蒂蒂亚·詹姆斯提起的一起民事诉讼中对做出不利于他的裁决。

sentences.en: James had accused Trump of fraud for inflating the value of his assets and seeks millions in damages.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯指控特朗普通过夸大资产价值进行欺诈，并寻求数百万美元的赔偿。

sentences.en: But the surprising court decision granted one of the biggest punishments James sought,
sentences.zh: 但这项令人惊讶的法院裁决支持了詹姆斯寻求的最严厉惩罚之一，

sentences.en: the cancellation of business certificates that allowed some of Mr. Trump's New York properties to operate.
sentences.zh: 取消了允许特朗普先生的一些纽约房产运营的商业证书。

sentences.en: That could terminate Trump's control over assets that include 40 Wall Street, a family estate, a golf club in Westchester County, and Trump Tower.
sentences.zh: 这可能会终结特朗普对包括华尔街40号、一处家族庄园、韦斯特切斯特县的高尔夫俱乐部和特朗普大厦在内的资产的控制权。

sentences.en: The ruling will almost certainly be appealed by Trump.
sentences.zh: 这项裁决几乎肯定会遭到特朗普的上诉。

sentences.en: And the Federal Trade Commission and 17 states sued Amazon, setting up a long-awaited antitrust fight that could alter the way Americans shop online.
sentences.zh: 联邦贸易委员会和17个州起诉了亚马逊，引发了一场期待已久的、可能会改变美国人网上购物方式的反垄断诉讼。

sentences.en: In the 172-page suit,
sentences.zh: 在这份172页的诉讼中，

sentences.en: the federal government accused the e-commerce giant of protecting a monopoly over swaths of online retail by squeezing merchants and favoring its own services.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府指控这家电商巨头通过挤压商家并偏袒自身服务，巩固了其对大片在线零售领域的垄断地位。

sentences.en: The suit alleges that the retailer's tactics made it impossible for its rivals to compete.
sentences.zh: 诉讼称，这家零售商的战术使得竞争对手根本无法与之竞争。

sentences.en: Finally, Ukraine acknowledged that there might be some uncertainty surrounding its claim that Russia's Black Sea Fleet commander was killed in a strike on Crimea.
sentences.zh: 最后，乌克兰承认，关于俄罗斯黑海舰队司令在克里米亚袭击中丧生的说法，可能存在一些不确定性。

sentences.en: Kiev said that it was, quote, clarifying whether Viktor Sokolov had in fact been killed.
sentences.zh: 基辅表示，正在，引述，“澄清维克托·索科洛夫是否真的阵亡”。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, Moscow released a video purporting to show the admiral alive.
sentences.zh: 周二，莫斯科发布了一段据称显示该海军上将还活着的视频。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Shannon Lynn, Summer Tamad, Sidney Harper, and Rochelle Bonja.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由香农·林恩、萨默·塔马德、西德尼·哈珀和罗谢尔·邦贾制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by M.J.
sentences.zh: 由M.J.·

sentences.en: Davis Lynn with help from Michael Barbaro, contains original music by Marianne Lozano and Will Reed, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯·林恩编辑，迈克尔·巴巴罗提供了帮助，包含玛丽安·洛扎诺和威尔·里德的原创音乐，由克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯福德创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔维内西。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称为改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱有时甚至惊心动魄的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《Metro》的最新一期节目中，我和萨拉·科尼格一起，讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《Metro》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在您获取播客的任何地方收听。
